title: session-sticky-a-b-scheduler-with-retrospective-mitigations
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a session-sticky A/B scheduling lane with retrospective mitigation hooks; adds telemetry for session-level divergence; exposes rollback playbook via API; non-breaking default behavior; opt-in via rollout config.
description: Motivation: Certain A/B experiments require session affinity (stickiness) across phased rollouts to avoid erratic UX when users bounce between model variants during an experiment. Operators also requested a way to surface and auto-apply retrospective mitigations when cohort-level regressions are detected after a roll-forward window. This PR implements a session-sticky A/B scheduler that pairs: (1) a lightweight session affinity token managed by the gateway, (2) a scheduler that respects session continuity when assigning variants, and (3) a retrospective-mitigation subsystem that computes cohort deltas over a lookback window and applies fast mitigations (traffic shrink, snapshot revert, or sample quarantine) via the rollout controller. Changes: 1) scheduler core: new SessionAffinityManager and AbSessionAllocator with pluggable hashing and TTL; 2) rollout engine: integration hooks for retrospective mitigation policies and a compact policy DSL; 3) telemetry: per-session trace ids, cohort-delta metrics, and an explainability tag emitted on mitigations; 4) API: /rollouts/{id}/mitigation-status and an admin endpoint to replay a retrospective decision; 5) docs/tests: unit, integration, and an end-to-end smoke harness with synthetic sessions. Safety model: default rollout configs remain unchanged unless session_affinity is enabled. Retrospective mitigations are opt-in and require an explicit mitigation_budget in the rollout spec. The subsystem is designed to only enact non-disruptive actions (traffic shrink by fraction, sample quarantine) unless the operator escalates to a full snapshot revert. Implementation notes: decided on deterministic allocation using siphash128 to avoid cross-language variance; affinity token is signed and has a 24h TTL by default; the allocator keeps a tiny cache to avoid recomputing for heavy tails. Testing: added unit tests for allocator boundary cases, integration tests exercising mitigations against the canary simulator, and a stress job that validates memory/latency under heavy session loads. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal customers for 2 weeks behind a feature flag, then gated beta with SLO checks (latency and quality delta thresholds) before global enablement. Backout plan: if any critical regression is seen, the mitigation subsystem can (a) instantly shrink variant traffic to 0% (fast path), (b) quarantine sessions for sampling and replay, or (c) initiate snapshot revert via the model registry integration. Related: linear ENG-1298 tracks product acceptance criteria; SUP-3421 is the support case that motivated retrospective mitigations. Checklist: - [x] core allocator implemented - [x] mitigation DSL and engine - [x] API and console hooks - [x] telemetry and alert rules - [x] tests and e2e harness - [x] docs and runbook Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the sticky logic out of the canonical decision graph to minimize risk to other rollout modes. Future work: add probabilistic decay for long sessions and automatic mitigation suggestions based on historical signal patterns.
